newsitem.title: USA: Nurses to strike Kaiser Permanente hospitals.
newsitem.headline: Nurses to strike Kaiser Permanente hospitals.

text.p: Thousands of nurses employed by the nation's largest health maintenance organisation, Kaiser Permanente, will walk off the job Thursday and Friday to protest the breakdown of contract negotiations, their union said Tuesday.

The strike is expected to involve 7,500 nurses at 47 northern California hospitals and clinics. The striking nurses say they expect to be joined by 17,000 other health care workers, housekeepers and clerical workers, represented by other unions.

Kaiser said it will have staff doctors and nurses supervisors fill in as nurses for the two days, and may move some of its southern California employees up to the San Francisco area to assure it is able to serve its patients.

The nurses, who are fighting proposed wage reductions, reduced staffing levels and deep reductions in their own health care benefits, say they also want to call attention to what they say is a diminishing quality of patient care at many Kaiser hospitals.

Rose Ann De Moro, executive director of the California Nurses Association, which is staging the strike, said Kaiser has tried to "devalue the profession of nursing" and displace some of its most experienced nurses with lower-paid, less-experienced ones.
She said these patterns have caused the quality of care in Kaiser hospitals to decline, resulting in long waits for emergency care and a shortage of specialised nurses on hand.

Kaiser, however, accuses the nurses' union of negotiating in bad faith. It said it returned to the bargaining table last week with strong concessions, including proposals for higher pay, but was still unable to reach an agreement with the nurses.

The California Nurses Association staged a similar one-day strike in April, and last year authored a ballot initiative imposing strict regulations on health maintenance organisations. Voters defeated that initiative.
